conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for coming in. I’m Dr. Carter, a perinatal mental-health clinician. My job is to check in on how moms are feeling after baby arrives, because the transition can bring lots of unexpected emotions.  

Today I’ll be using a quick tool called the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It’s ten questions about how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays between us unless safety is a concern. We’ll just talk through each item together; you answer in your own words and we’ll take it at your pace.

Ready to start?  

Here’s the first question:  
Over the last seven days, when you were able to laugh and see the funny side of things, how often did you feel that actually happened?

I’ve still found myself laughing at a few things—like when my husband tried to swaddle the baby and put the blanket on upside-down. It’s not the same constant giggles I used to have, but I do laugh… maybe once or twice a day.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Most of the time I can still laugh, just not as easily as before the baby. It feels a little forced sometimes, but I do get moments—especially when my husband makes his silly faces—where it feels natural.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few things—like my morning coffee or when my mom comes over to help—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of really counting down the hours like I did before.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday the baby was extra fussy and I kept thinking maybe I ate something that upset her stomach, or that I wasn’t soothing her the “right” way. I know logically babies just cry, but I still caught myself wondering what I did wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll be sitting on the couch, everything quiet, and suddenly my heart feels a little racing—like I forgot something important, even though I can’t think of anything. It passes pretty fast if I take a few deep breaths or look at the baby and see she’s fine, but yeah, it pops up a few times a day for no real reason.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panic, but there have been a couple of moments—like when I was grocery shopping and suddenly felt hot and kind of dizzy, and my mind jumped to “what if I pass out and something happens to the baby?” It lasted maybe a minute, then I calmed myself down, but it was unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. When the baby won’t nap and the laundry’s piled up, I feel like I’m drowning a little. I usually get through it once she finally settles, but I’ll think, “How am I going to keep doing this every day?”
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’ve been tired enough that I fall asleep okay once the baby’s down. Once in a while I’ll lie there running through the day in my head—like did I burp her long enough, did I sterilize the bottles right—but it’s not every night and I still drift off within maybe twenty minutes.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I’d say a few times this week—mostly in the evenings when the house is quiet and I’m by myself feeding her. It’s not crying-every-day sad, just this heavy “blah” feeling that lingers for a little while before I distract myself with a show or scroll on my phone.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried twice—once on Tuesday when she wouldn’t latch and I felt like my body was failing her, and then yesterday when I dropped a plate and it shattered. Both times I teared up for maybe five minutes, wiped my face, and moved on.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’m tired and sometimes overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Patient: Post-delivery mother (≈ 2–6 wks PP, per narrative)

Symptoms & Observations  
• Persistent low mood: reports “heavy ‘blah’” most evenings, crying twice/week, diminished enjoyment (“that’ll be nice” vs prior excitement)  
• Anhedonia: laughter feels “forced,” pleasure blunted  
• Excessive guilt / self-blame: attributes infant fussiness to personal error  
• Generalized & situational anxiety: daily “racing heart,” two near-panic episodes while shopping  
• Feeling overwhelmed: “drowning” when routine tasks accumulate  
• Sleep onset possible only after rumination; no frank insomnia  
• NO self-harm ideation

Pattern  
Mild–moderate depressive symptoms with comorbid anxiety; functional impact limited but present; no safety concerns identified today.

Screening Significance  
Meets partial criteria for minor/major depressive episode with anxious features; Edinburgh score likely 10–12 range (informal). Continue monitoring; consider formal diagnostic interview if symptoms persist > 2 wks or worsen.
